component_postures.basis: USDA Grain Transportation Report documented VLSFO near $960/metric ton on March 11, up 79% in two weeks, and IFO 380 reaching an all-time high March 9.
USDA documented higher U.S. Gulf-to-Japan and Pacific Northwest-to-Japan grain ocean freight rates during the same shock interval.
BLS March PPI documented a 42.0% monthly increase in No. 2 diesel fuel within processed intermediate demand.
BLS recorded March transportation/warehousing price pressure and USDA later documented materially higher rail fuel surcharges tied to diesel cost conditions.
Food CPI was flat in March, then rose 0.5% in April, 0.2% in May, 0.2% in June, and 0.1% in July. This supports later consumer-food movement but not sole attribution to shipping fuel.

Under the frozen CPI consumer-category comparator and the primary March 9-11 marine-fuel-shock clock, food was not the first downstream consumer category to show material movement. In March food at home fell 0.2% while apparel rose 1.0% and transportation services rose 0.6%; in April food at home rose 0.7%, but household furnishings also rose 0.7% and apparel rose 0.6%.
Current preserved first-party text does not authorize an exclusivity claim, and observed food prices have multiple contemporaneous causal inputs.
